svg.title: What you can use harness-evals for
svg.desc: Six use cases, each with code. 1: agent or workflow, run both and compare; in the refund-desk example the workflow is adopted because the agent broke the refund policy in 2 of 50 runs. 2: did a prompt or tool change help; compare two versions, inconclusive means keep the base and add tasks or runs. 3: a cheaper harness is adopted within a margin when every cost is known. 4: compare saved runs from the CLI; manifests must match. 5: calibrate an LLM judge against human labels with agreement(). 6: failures() counts failing checks per task to show which traces to read first.
svg.text: What you can use it for
Six questions harness-evals answers, and the code that asks each one.
is a plain workflow good enough?
the agent broke the refund policy
a new prompt, tool or routing rule
no clear benefit yet: keep v1,
fewer model calls, a smaller context
only when every run of both
later, from the CLI or in CI
read the most frequent failure first
